title: Reads the Same Both Ways
statement:
Given a string s, decide whether it reads the same forwards and backwards once you look only at the characters that count.

A character counts if it is an ASCII letter (a–z, A–Z) or an ASCII digit (0–9). Everything else is ignored: spaces, punctuation, underscores and so on. Letters are compared without case, so "A" and "a" are equal. Digits count too; they are not dropped.

Return true if the counted characters form a palindrome, otherwise false. If no character counts, the answer is true.

examples.why: The counted characters are "steponnopets", which is the same reversed. Comparing the raw string would fail on the spaces, the "!" and the capital S.
The counted characters are "1bb2". Dropping the digits would leave "bb" and wrongly say true.
Nothing counts, and an empty sequence reads the same both ways.

args: Was it a car or a cat I saw?

hints: The easy version builds a cleaned copy and compares it with its reverse. That works. Can you avoid the copy?
Put one pointer at each end. What should a pointer do when it sits on a character that does not count?
Skip non-counting characters from both ends, then compare the two characters in lower case. Any mismatch means false; if the pointers meet, it is true.

explain.intuition:
A palindrome check compares the first character with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and so on. Two pointers walking inward do exactly that. The only twist is the noise: a pointer that lands on a space or a comma just steps past it, because that character does not take part in the comparison.

This avoids building a second string, so the extra memory is O(1). In JavaScript there is no built-in isalnum, so you need a small test such as /[a-z0-9]/i.
steps: While lo < hi: if s[lo] does not count, move lo right and continue. Same for s[hi], moving left.
Both pointers now sit on counted characters. Compare them in lower case. If they differ, return false.
Otherwise move both inward and repeat. When the loop ends, return true.
pitfalls: Treating only letters as counted. Digits count: "1b, B2" is not a palindrome.
Skipping a non-counted character without re-checking lo < hi: in ",. ;" the pointers can run past each other and read outside the string.
Comparing without lowering the case: "Aa" is a palindrome.

solutions.title: Clean, then compare with the reverse
solutions.idea: Keep only the counted characters in lower case and compare that string with its reverse. Short and clear, but it builds two extra strings.

solutions.title: Two pointers from the ends
solutions.idea: Walk inward from both ends, skipping characters that do not count and comparing the rest in lower case.

followups: You may delete at most one counted character. Can the string still become a palindrome?
The text arrives as a stream you can read only once, left to right. What would you need to store?
